issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the lower bound in (P1) for n in (undertilde n, n_tilde] uses sigma_{n_tilde}(f_n) >= sigma_{n_tilde+1}(f_{n_tilde+1}). The algorithm only guarantees the weak-greedy choice for the first element of each batch; for the remaining parallel elements no property ensures that their distance after the full batch dominates the distance of the next batch's first element. The displayed chain therefore contains an unjustified and generally false inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either change the selection of the remaining b-1 batch elements so that a valid diagonal lower bound holds, or prove a replacement property for the stated parallel selection, and then rederive all dependent rate estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The central convergence estimates for the weak batch greedy algorithm are unsupported. All Hilbert-space and Banach-space batch greedy rate results depending on (P1) become unreliable.
issues.title: Batch diagonal lower bound (P1) is not proved for non-first batch elements
issues.why_classification: The defect attacks the core property needed for the batch convergence analysis. No local correction preserves the advertised parallel batch algorithm and its rate guarantees without a new selection rule or nontrivial argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for every $m \geq n$ one has $\sum_{j=n}^m a_{m,j}^2 \leq \sigma_n$

issues.failure_explanation: Property (P2) as stated gives only ||g_i||^2 <= sigma_{n+1}, hence ||g_i|| <= sqrt(sigma_{n+1}), not ||g_i|| <= sigma_{n+1}. The needed bound follows from the squared distance estimate, but the proof cites the weaker (P2) and does not make that step explicit.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen (P2) to sum_{j=n}^m a_{m,j}^2 <= sigma_n^2, or directly note that ||g_i||^2 = dist(f_{n+i}, V_{n+1})^2 <= sigma_{n+1}^2, so that ||g_i|| <= sigma_{n+1}.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the Hilbert product estimate is not fully justified; downstream rate estimates relying on it are affected until the proof gap is closed.
issues.title: Hilbert theorem proof uses an insufficient form of (P2)
issues.why_classification: This is a local proof repair that preserves all stated conclusions and rates.

The stated C_1(M,b) uses M, not s, and need not satisfy the required inequality. Thus the proof establishes a different, fixed or larger constant, not the stated n-dependent one.

In the first-violation argument at M = ceil(2+(b-1)/s) s, the required contradiction needs c_1(M,b) to be bounded by an s-dependent quantity; the stated c_1(M,b) uses M and does not guarantee this. Additionally, the term ln(C_1)b^{-alpha} can be negative when C_1 < 1, in which case the displayed Case 3 inequality C_1 e^{-c_1 b^alpha} >= 1 is not valid as a positive decay constant argument.

The subsequent monotonicity direction is therefore invalid. Separately, the displayed equality replaces 2 sqrt(C_0) gamma^{-1} by C_1 = sqrt(2 C_0) gamma^{-1}, which is false. The n-dependent c_1(n,b) is also not consistently justified.
